prerequisites: Average knowledge of high school mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Master matrix algebra as the basis for many engineering-relevant calculation methods (eigenvalue calculation, FEM, kinematics, fluid dynamics, electrical engineering).
Master differential calculus with several variables and integral calculus with two variables.
Understand differential equations as a representation of real technical systems.
Assess the Laplace transformation for calculating system behavior and explain its meaning.
Independently find problem-solving hints in provided documents and other sources.
Question the correctness of proposed solutions.
Process tasks in a structured and creative manner.

syllabus_topics: Differential and Integral Calculus with several variables
Extraction of mathematical relationships from problems in mechanics, physics, electrical engineering, manufacturing technology
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written exam (passing grade). The weight of the grade for the final grade is determined by the Bachelor's examination regulations.
